verses.1:1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: We must always give thanks to God for you, brothers, just as is fitting, because your faith is growing exceedingly, and the love of each one of you toward one another is abounding,
verses.1:4: so that we ourselves also boast of you in the churches of God, for your patience and faith, and in all your persecutions and afflictions that you are enduring,
verses.1:5: as an example of the just judgment of God, so that you may be considered worthy in the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer;
verses.1:6: if indeed it is just with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you,
verses.1:7: and to you who are afflicted, rest with us at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of His power,
verses.1:8: in a flame of fire, rendering vengeance to those who do not know God and who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.1:9: who will pay eternal penalties in destruction, away from the face of the Lord and from the glory of His power,
verses.1:10: when He comes to be glorified in His saints, and to become wondrous in all who have believed, because our testimony to you was believed, on that day.
verses.1:11: In this also we always pray for you, that our God may deem you worthy of His calling, and fulfill every desire of goodness and the work of faith in power,
verses.1:12: so that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in Him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2:1: Now we ask you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and of our gathering together to Him,
verses.2:2: that you not be quickly moved from your mind, nor be frightened, either by a spirit, or by a word, or by a letter as though sent through us, as if the day of the Lord were imminent.
verses.2:3: Let no one deceive you in any way, because unless the falling away comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition,
verses.2:4: who opposes and lifts himself up above everything that is called God or that is worshiped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as though he were God.
verses.2:5: Do you not recall that when I was still with you, I used to tell you these things?
verses.2:6: And now you know what restrains, so that he may be revealed in his own time.
verses.2:7: For the mystery of wickedness is already at work; only that the one who now restrains must keep restraining until he is removed from the midst.
verses.2:8: And then that wicked one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill by the breath of His mouth, and by the brilliance of His coming He will destroy him,
verses.2:9: whose coming is according to Satan's working, in all power and signs and lying wonders,
verses.2:10: and in every deception of wickedness for those who are perishing, because they did not accept the love of the truth so that they might be saved.
verses.2:11: For this reason God will send them a working of error, so that they may believe a lie,
verses.2:12: in order that all may be judged who did not believe the truth, but consented to wickedness.
verses.2:13: But we must always give thanks to God for you, brothers loved by God, because God chose you as firstfruits for salvation in the sanctification of the Spirit and in faith in the truth,
verses.2:14: in which He also called you through our gospel, for the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.2:15: So then, brothers, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you learned, whether by word or by our letter.
verses.2:16: Now may our Lord Jesus Christ Himself, and God and our Father, who loved us and gave eternal comfort and good hope in grace,
verses.2:17: encourage your hearts and strengthen them in every good work and word.
verses.3:1: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of God may run and be glorified, just as it also is among you,
verses.3:2: and that we may be rescued from unreasonable and evil men, for faith does not belong to all.
verses.3:3: But God is faithful; He will strengthen you and guard you from evil.
verses.3:4: And we have confidence about you in the Lord, that what we instructed, you are both doing and will do.
verses.3:5: And may the Lord direct your hearts in the love of God and the patience of Christ.
verses.3:6: Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw yourselves from every brother walking in a disorderly way and not according to the tradition that they received from us.
verses.3:7: For you yourselves know how one ought to imitate us, because we were not restless among you,
verses.3:8: nor did we eat bread for free from anyone, but in labor and in fatigue, working night and day, so that we might not burden any of you.
verses.3:9: Not as though we did not have authority, but so that we might give ourselves to you as a pattern for imitating us.
verses.3:10: For even when we were with you, we kept commanding you this, that if anyone does not want to work, neither should he eat.
verses.3:11: For we have heard that some among you are walking restlessly, working at nothing, but acting meddlesomely.
verses.3:12: Now let us command those who are of this kind, and we urge them in the Lord Jesus Christ, that working with quietness they eat their own bread.
verses.3:13: But you, brothers, do not lose heart in doing good.
verses.3:14: And if anyone does not obey our word through the letter, take note of him, and do not associate with him, so that he may be ashamed;
verses.3:15: and do not regard him as an enemy, but reprove him as a brother.
verses.3:16: Now may the Lord of peace Himself give you everlasting peace in every place. The Lord be with all of you.
verses.3:17: The greeting, with my own hand, Paul's, which is the sign in every letter; this is how I write.
verses.3:18: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.

notes.1:5: Vulgate reads in exemplum ('as an example', where Greek has endeigma, 'evidence/proof') and in regno Dei ('in the kingdom of God', where Greek has the genitive 'of the kingdom of God').
notes.1:9: Vulgate reads poenas ... in interitu aeternas ('eternal penalties in destruction'), attaching 'eternal' to 'penalties' and placing 'in destruction' in a prepositional phrase, whereas Greek has 'the penalty of eternal destruction'.
notes.1:10: Vulgate renders Greek thaumasthenai ('to be marveled at') with the adjective-plus-verb construction admirabilis fieri ('to become wondrous').
notes.2:1: Vulgate uses the preposition of appeal per adventum ('by the coming') rather than Greek hyper ('concerning'), while retaining the genitive nostrae congregationis ('and of our gathering together').
notes.2:2: Vulgate explicitly adds missam ('sent') to tamquam per nos and renders Greek enesteken ('has already come') with instet ('were imminent' or 'at hand').
notes.2:3: Vulgate reads discessio ('the falling away' or 'departure/defection') and homo peccati ('the man of sin'), matching the Byzantine Greek reading (hamartias) rather than critical Greek editions (anomias, 'of lawlessness').
notes.2:7: Vulgate uses iniquitas ('wickedness/iniquity') across 2:7, 10, 12 and ille iniquus ('that wicked one') in 2:8, uniting Greek anomia/anomos and adikia; it also supplies the explicit subjunctive tantum ut ... teneat ('only that ... must keep restraining') and the idiom de medio fiat ('be removed from the midst').
notes.2:13: Vulgate reads a Deo ('by God', where Greek has 'by the Lord') and primitias ('as firstfruits', reflecting the Greek variant aparchen rather than ap' arches, 'from the beginning').
notes.3:1: Vulgate reads sermo Dei ('the word of God'), whereas Greek manuscripts read 'the word of the Lord'.
notes.3:3: Vulgate reads Deus ('God'), whereas most Greek manuscripts read 'the Lord'. Latin a malo can be understood as either neuter ('from evil') or masculine ('from the evil one').
notes.3:6: Vulgate reads third-person plural acceperunt ('they received'), referring collectively to 'every brother', and shifts from inordinate ('in a disorderly way') here to inquieti/inquiete ('restless/restlessly') in 3:7 and 3:11.
notes.3:12: The Clementine Vulgate reads the present subjunctive denuntiemus ('let us command') alongside the indicative obsecramus ('and we urge'), where Greek has two indicatives.
notes.3:16: Vulgate reads pacem sempiternam ('everlasting peace', where Greek has 'peace at all times') and in omni loco ('in every place', reflecting the Greek variant en panti topo rather than en panti tropo, 'in every way').
